ship.header: Captain's log, stardate 80240.9. Gishath, Sun's Avatar; the list carries no tagged version.
ship.situation: We put in at Alex's house on Moraga Way in Orinda on the evening of Friday the twenty-eighth. This was the fourth and final engagement of the evening, taken up directly after Heliod came off the line. Two vessels in the sector, under Alex and under Stuart respectively.
ship.narrative: We developed our resources ahead of their early removal and were never behind on lands. The table then spent its board-clearing spells on the middle of our formation, and we replaced those bodies faster than the answers arrived; when our own side of the board stood empty we cast Blasphemous Act and cleared theirs at no cost to ourselves. That asymmetry ran the length of the game. Gishath came down and struck at Stuart for seven, and the trigger turned over seven cards and found five dinosaurs, one of which caused their creatures to arrive tapped, so no formation opposite us could be assembled. The following turn we drew Enlarge, added seven and seven, and struck for fourteen; with the seven already carried, the damage from our own commander stood at twenty-one and the seat was lost. The second trigger turned over fourteen cards, found two more dinosaurs, and one of them refilled our hand. We made no changes to the ship afterwards.

assessment.text: I would not record this as a piloting victory. My decisions were unremarkable and largely obvious; the line was open, and I walked down it. The one judgment I will claim is holding Blasphemous Act until our own board was bare, and it is not much of a claim.

The ship worked as designed, which is worth stating plainly because it is not always so. The middle of the deck absorbed the answers aimed at it, and the commander and its trigger — which are the actual threat aboard — arrived against a table with nothing left to spend.

The table misjudged the tiers of threat in front of it. They committed their board-clearing spells to creatures that were, in effect, screening for the commander, and were empty-handed when it landed. That is a reading of theirs rather than a design of mine, and I would not expect to be offered it twice.

orders.text: I have ordered Helm to alter nothing. The record supports no change, and a night that went this way is a poor moment to make one.

I have instructed Tactical to enter in its own report that the middle of our formation drew the table's answers on this occasion, and to plan on the assumption that it will not do so once the tiers are read correctly.

ship.coda: There was a good deal of laughter at the table, most of it directed at the reading rather than at the result. Nelson held that no captain can do very wrong who lays his ship alongside that of the enemy; on this occasion the enemy declined to notice which ship it was.
